did: The planner split the ask into six stories, 25 criteria in all.
Each criterion quotes the owner's words from the issue or comment.
decided: A build's turn ends when the other story's pull request merges or closes.
A story is big when it holds more than five criteria.
open: Three questions wait for the owner: big story size, when a turn ends, closing #553.

handback.summary: Every ask has a criterion; one normal case is missing: a build starting after the other story merges.

raises.label: S4.1 missing case
raises.text: Criterion 4.1 lists only an unmerged close ending the wait. Add the normal case: the other story merges, and the waiting build starts.
raises.evidence: plan.json, story 4, criterion 1 edge_cases holds one case: closes unmerged.

asks.ask: The planner tags each criterion with the code files it changes.
Each criterion carries a `files` list in the plan's structured output: the code files it changes, at least one.
Code rejects a plan where a criterion lists none.
A file it creates counts by its path.
A criterion lists every file its behavior needs, never just one, so a behavior is never cut across stories.
if it can be written as code (infrastructure as code, a setup script), it's a criterion like any other.
The plan's scope is all criteria's files plus their tests
with no separate scope field.
The fence keeps enforcing it.
Each one quotes my words, which are the spec.
Code groups criteria that share any code file into one story (a sub-issue).
Criteria with no file in common become separate stories.
No number decides it: no criteria cap, no story cap.
This replaces today's count-based split rules (split above 3 criteria per story, refuse above 15 per issue).
Markdown files never group criteria
Edge cases stay under their criterion and don't affect the split.
Stories that share a file wait their turn to build.
Planning and plan review never wait; only the worker's build does.
and never make a story wait.
Stories merge to main one by one. No parent branch.
A step that changes no file (clicking through a console, for example) is listed on the plan as mine to do.
it's a step for me on the plan, and the stories that build on it are blocked by it until I close it.
Nothing waits on it by itself.
Red first stays: every criterion's test fails on main before work starts.
An ask that can't be checked becomes a question to me
or shows on the card as not verified.
When a story is big because many criteria share one file, the card names that file.
